meta.title: Who Pays When the Agent Buys
meta.summary: Agents can now shop and pay. Nineteen protocols compete to carry those payments, few move real money yet, and the rules on who pays for a wrong purchase are only starting to form. What each protocol decides, how far it has shipped, and what to build first.
meta.artifact_title: Who Pays When the Agent Buys
plain: Mandate
The user's signed approval of what the agent may buy
Agentic or network token
A stand in card number made for one agent
PSP
Your payment provider, such as Stripe or Adyen
HTTP 402
A built in web code that asks for payment
Facilitator
The service that settles a pay per call payment
Webhook
A message one system sends another when something happens
HMAC, RFC 9421
Two ways to sign a message so changes show
SD-JWT
A signed credential that reveals only chosen fields
KYA
Know your agent, checking who runs an agent
SCA
EU rule that asks for two proofs of identity
EMVCo
The body that sets shared card standards

layers.name: Discover
layers.one: Agents find products and what each merchant's checkout supports.
layers.arch: Product feeds, well known capability files, MCP servers and Agent Cards tell agents what they can buy and how.

layers.name: Intent and mandate
layers.one: Proof of what the user allowed the agent to buy.
layers.arch: Token limits, signed open or closed mandates, or instructions the network holds. None defines a dispute process.

layers.name: Agent identity
layers.one: Lets a merchant tell a trusted agent from a bot.
layers.arch: Mostly RFC 9421 signed requests checked against a key directory, plus network registration or KYA tokens.

layers.name: Credential
layers.one: What pays, without handing card numbers to the agent.
layers.arch: Agentic network tokens, PSP scoped tokens, wallet accounts, stablecoin keys or bank account mandates such as UPI Reserve Pay.

layers.name: Rail
layers.one: How the money moves, and how fast and costly.
layers.arch: Card networks, real time bank rails, stablecoins on chain or Lightning. Each sets cost, speed and reversibility.

layers.name: Settle
layers.one: Money lands, and both sides reconcile the order.
layers.arch: Acquirers settle cards. Facilitators verify and settle HTTP 402 payments on chain, some batching many into one.

layers.name: Dispute
layers.one: Who refunds or absorbs a bad agent purchase.
layers.arch: Card reason codes written for human buyers, mandates offered as evidence, and no dispute path on chain rails.

usecases.name: Consumer checkout
usecases.one: A person's agent buys from a merchant with card or wallet.

usecases.name: B2B procurement
usecases.one: A business agent pays suppliers or invoices within limits a human set.

usecases.name: Machine pay per call
usecases.one: An agent pays per API call, tool call or page.

protocols.name: ACP
protocols.one: Simple REST checkout. It has gone quiet, and ChatGPT now sends buyers to retailer sites.
protocols.arch: Merchant feed, checkout sessions, then delegated payment returns a token capped by amount, merchant and expiry. Idempotency keys required. No agent identity scheme. Copilot Checkout used it for Stripe sellers at launch.
protocols.gaps: No signed user mandate, one time allowance only, no release since April.

params.P5: PSP scoped token or network token

protocols.name: UCP
protocols.owner: Google and Shopify, with Stripe and councils
protocols.one: The only checkout protocol with verified live consumer checkout in the last 90 days, via Google Universal Cart.
protocols.arch: Business profile and keys at a well known file, optional signed requests, checkout over REST, MCP, A2A or embedded. An optional AP2 mandate extension locks the session once negotiated.
protocols.gaps: Nothing tagged since August, both 2026 releases broke old versions. No B2B or pay per call.

params.P5: wallet account, PSP or network token

protocols.name: AP2
protocols.one: Signed mandates that prove what the user allowed, for purchases with or without them present.
protocols.arch: Open Checkout and Payment mandates set limits ahead, closed ones bind one cart. SD-JWT credentials with the agent key bound in. Transport left to UCP or A2A.
protocols.gaps: No release since April. Disputes out of scope. Signatures can sit on manipulated choices.

params.P11: not defined, runs inside UCP or A2A

protocols.name: A2A
protocols.one: Messaging between agents across companies. Commerce comes only through extensions such as x402.
protocols.arch: Signed Agent Cards for discovery and long running tasks. The x402 extension adds payment states and an append only receipts list, but has seen little work.
protocols.gaps: No commerce meaning in core. Extension has no spend limits or mandate link.

params.P1: machine to machine or not present

protocols.name: MCP
protocols.full: Model Context Protocol, WebMCP and Shop MCP
protocols.one: How agents call tools. Shopify runs live checkout on it, and paid tools wrap x402 or MPP.
protocols.arch: Stateless spec with no payment primitive. Shop MCP completes checkout only after the shopper confirms. AWS AgentCore pays for MCP tools over x402 and MPP.
protocols.gaps: No payment object, no mandate, no standard human confirmation for paid tool calls.

params.P1: human present or machine to machine

protocols.name: Web Bot Auth
protocols.full: IETF Web Bot Auth over RFC 9421
protocols.owner: IETF working group, Cloudflare and Google authors
protocols.one: Signed requests that prove which agent called. ChatGPT's browser already signs with it.
protocols.arch: Agent publishes keys at a well known address and signs each request. Verifiers fetch the directory and check the signature. Proves the agent, not the user's consent.
protocols.gaps: Not yet an RFC. Card network tags differ from the draft's single tag.

protocols.name: Visa TAP
protocols.one: Visa's agent identity check, now in a live B2B invoice pilot with BILL and Billtrust.
protocols.arch: Registered agents sign each request with RFC 9421 and a browse or pay tag. Merchant or CDN verifies against a Visa hosted key directory and a replay cache.
protocols.gaps: No versioned spec, sample repo idle, tags differ from the IETF draft.

params.P3: signed HTTP requests, network registered agent

protocols.name: Verifiable Intent
protocols.one: A signed record of what the cardholder asked for, shown in parts to each party.
protocols.arch: Chained SD-JWT layers bound to device and agent keys. The network sees payment data, the merchant sees checkout data. Fields align to AP2.
protocols.gaps: Still a first draft with one maintainer and no verified production use.

protocols.name: KYAPay and KYA
protocols.full: Know Your Agent tokens and framework
protocols.owner: Skyfire draft, Ant, Mastercard and Visa framework
protocols.one: A trusted issuer vouches for the agent and its human in a signed token.
protocols.arch: KYAPay carries identity and payment claims in JWTs sent in a request header. The cross network KYA framework has no spec or timeline.
protocols.gaps: Individual draft only. The trusted issuer list is out of scope.

params.P1: not present or machine to machine

protocols.name: FIDO, EMVCo, OpenID
protocols.full: Standards body work on agent identity and intent
protocols.one: Where mandate and agent authentication standards are expected to settle. No public draft yet.
protocols.arch: FIDO groups seeded with AP2 and Verifiable Intent, chaired by Mastercard and Visa for payments. EMVCo drafted intent services and is exploring agent checks. AuthZEN covers approvals.
protocols.gaps: No timeline from FIDO. EMVCo text seen only through trade press.

protocols.name: Visa Intelligent Commerce
protocols.one: Gives each agent its own Visa token after a passkey. Live, with volume Visa calls limited.
protocols.arch: Token provisioned through Visa Token Service, instructions sent as an encrypted payload. Connect accepts TAP, MPP, ACP and UCP. No agentic volume published.
protocols.gaps: No agentic fee or volume disclosed. Cardholders answer for enrolled agents under Visa rules.

protocols.name: Agent Pay
protocols.full: Mastercard Agent Pay and Agent Pay for Machines
protocols.one: Agentic Mastercard tokens for registered agents. Live in Shop Pay and several markets, volumes small.
protocols.arch: Agent registers, signs requests through Web Bot Auth, and pays with an agentic token in the normal card form. Issuer authorises, with a passkey where needed.
protocols.gaps: No GA statement or agent liability rule found. Machines product has no real money.

params.P3: network registered agent, signed HTTP requests

protocols.name: Amex ACE
protocols.one: Promises agent error cover, not yet live. Intent Intelligence has no live integrations.
protocols.arch: Intent Intelligence, published 2026-10-13, carries the purchase intent registered agents send Amex. Agent Purchase Protection is promised, not yet available.
protocols.gaps: No live integration yet. Protection terms and developer kit status not confirmed.

protocols.name: Stripe SPT
protocols.full: Stripe Shared Payment Tokens and Link
protocols.one: A scoped grant of the buyer's saved payment method to one seller, capped and revocable.
protocols.arch: Limits on currency, amount and expiry. Stripe may ride Visa or Mastercard agentic tokens underneath. Still under preview terms. Link balance spends USDC through a card.
protocols.gaps: No agent signature in the token flow. Link makes users answer for agent purchases.

protocols.name: x402
protocols.one: Pay per web request with stablecoins. Live, small, and down sharply since August.
protocols.arch: Server answers 402 with terms, client signs a stablecoin payment and retries, the server verifies, serves, then settles through a facilitator. Upto and batch settlement are merged.
protocols.gaps: No protocol refund or dispute path. Papers show unpaid service and paid but denied outcomes.

protocols.name: MPP
protocols.one: Pay per web request across many methods, from stablecoins to cards. Much smaller on chain.
protocols.arch: Charge, session and subscription intents. Methods include Tempo, Stripe, Lightning and Solana, with no ACH. Card payments settle off chain and are not counted.
protocols.gaps: IETF draft expired without working group adoption.

params.P5: stablecoin key, PSP token or card
params.P7: final on chain, chargeback on card

protocols.name: UPI agents
protocols.one: Users approve one spending limit per merchant, then the agent orders without repeated PIN prompts.
protocols.arch: UPI Reserve Pay blocks funds for several debits under a user approved limit. Piloted on Claude with Zomato, Swiggy and Zepto for a small group.
protocols.gaps: A wider agent protocol is reported, not confirmed. Liability and limits pending.

protocols.name: Pix agents
protocols.full: Pix agent payments through Iniciador MCP
protocols.owner: Banco Central do Brasil rail, Iniciador agent layer
protocols.one: Agents start Pix payments, and the user approves each one by device biometric.
protocols.arch: Iniciador's MCP server lets bank and fintech agents start Pix payments. Pix Automatico is a live recurring mandate rail on its own.
protocols.gaps: Launch status unstated and no volume disclosed.

protocols.name: Alipay and AMP
protocols.full: Alipay AI Pay and Ant AMP
protocols.one: The largest reported base, with explicit user approval for every payment. Figures are self reported.
protocols.arch: AI Pay installs into agents after an identity check. AI Wallet sits between user and agent. Ant's AMP runs on Alipay+ wallets.
protocols.gaps: Vendor figures only. AMP has no disclosed volumes or go live dates.

flows.name: Token checkout
flows.one: The agent never sees the card. A wallet or network hands the merchant a scoped token.
flows.arch: Discovery file or feed, signed agent request, buyer confirmation, then a single use network or PSP token charged through the merchant's own PSP. Disputes follow card reason codes.

steps.msg: Reads merchant profile and catalog
Signs request with registered agent key
Confirms total and payment method
Issues single use network token
Authorises token on card network
Sends order events to the agent
Handles disputes under card reason codes

flows.name: Signed mandate
flows.one: The user signs limits ahead, the agent signs the cart, and both become evidence.
flows.arch: Open mandate on a trusted surface binds the agent key. The agent signs a closed mandate over the cart hash. Credential provider checks both before issuing a token.

steps.msg: Signs open mandate on trusted surface
Builds cart with the merchant
Signs closed mandate bound to cart
Checks agent key in the mandate
Verifies mandates and issues payment token
Verifies bindings and returns signed receipts
Keeps mandates and receipts as evidence

flows.name: HTTP 402 pay per call
flows.one: The server asks for payment in its reply, and the agent pays and retries.
flows.arch: A 402 reply carries the price. The wallet checks its cap, signs and retries. The server verifies, serves, then settles through a facilitator. Payment is final.

steps.msg: Calls a paid API or tool
Replies 402 with price and payee
Checks the spend cap
Signs stablecoin payment authorisation
Verifies the signed payment for the server
Serves the data, settles, returns receipt
No protocol dispute path, refund by agreement

params.name: Initiator presence
params.why: Sets whether step up is possible and how disputes are judged.

params.name: Payer type
params.why: Picks the legal regime, consumer rules or business contract.

params.name: Agent identity method
values: CDN verified bot, Direct or Intermediary
params.why: Lets a merchant tell a trusted agent from a bot.

params.name: Mandate type
params.why: Decides what proof exists that the user agreed.

params.name: Credential
params.why: Decides who can see and reuse the payment detail.

params.name: Rail
params.why: Sets cost, speed, reach and reversibility.

params.name: Finality
params.why: Decides who absorbs a bad purchase.

params.name: Merchant of record
params.who: Contract, set by the agent platform's checkout
params.why: Owns tax, refunds and customer service.

params.name: Dispute path
params.why: Card reason codes were written for human buyers.

params.name: Liability holder
values: cardholder for an enrolled agent on Visa
params.why: The open question that slows adoption.

params.name: Transport
params.why: Sets who must change their stack.

params.name: Crypto primitive
params.why: Decides what can be verified offline and by whom.

params.name: Discovery
params.why: An agent cannot buy what it cannot find.

params.name: Jurisdiction
params.why: Consent, refund and liability rules differ by country.

params.name: Merchant authenticity check
params.why: Agents have paid fake stores in tests. P3 checks only the agent.

params.name: Agent access policy
params.why: Merchants now publish opposite rules on which agents may browse or buy.

params.name: Checkout location
values: merchant site through an agent browser
params.why: Decides where the buyer's final page lives, which transport alone does not say.

params.name: Consent capture surface
values: trusted surface such as a wallet or OS
params.why: Decides who can prove consent. A bot signature is not consent.

params.name: Agent signal at authorization
values: agentic network token with agent header
PSP token riding an agentic token
params.who: Network and PSP, agent platform picks
params.why: Stored cards hide the agent, so the issuer cannot apply agent risk controls.

params.name: Buyer identity and account linking
params.who: Merchant offers, agent platform chooses, user consents
params.why: Keeps loyalty and the customer record with the merchant.

params.name: Mandate enforcement point
params.why: Tells the merchant which checks it must run and which it cannot.

vars.name: Spend limit
vars.typical: per payment, per period, per merchant
vars.why: Caps loss when the agent errs. Only the platform or network sees every merchant.

vars.name: Expiry
vars.typical: minutes to months, and different at each layer
vars.why: Shorter expiry lowers the stolen credential window. Lifetimes differ by layer.
vars.who: Protocol and the issuer of each layer

vars.name: Scope
vars.why: Stops the right amount being spent on the wrong thing.

vars.name: Revocation
vars.why: A mandate must not outlive the user's intent.

vars.name: Step up threshold
vars.typical: amount or risk score that forces a passkey or approval

vars.name: Idempotency key and retries
vars.why: Stops double charges when an agent retries.

vars.name: Order events
vars.why: The agent must tell the user what happened.

vars.name: Evidence retention
vars.typical: mandate, cart, agent id, logs, kept for the rail's dispute window, then deleted

vars.name: Fees
vars.typical: card fees, gas, protocol fee, agent platform fee per sale
vars.why: Decides which use cases pay off.

vars.name: Latency budget
vars.why: Pay per call needs sub second settlement.

vars.name: Pre signing context capture
vars.typical: none, cart only, cart plus offers and ranking shown
vars.why: A valid signature can sit on a manipulated choice.

vars.name: Agent model and version recorded
vars.typical: not recorded, in the mandate, in the receipt
vars.why: Model updates change what agents buy, and users rarely notice.

vars.name: Revocation evidence
vars.typical: user record, platform signed notice, issuer or network registry
vars.why: A bank now makes customers prove they revoked an agent.

vars.name: Settlement mode
vars.typical: per payment, metered session, batched with upto or batch settlement, or authorize then capture, through a network, PSP, facilitator or wallet provider
vars.why: Cost, latency and concentration sit in how and through whom payments settle.

vars.name: Minimum ticket
vars.typical: smallest amount the PSP or facilitator will settle per payment
vars.why: Decides which use cases are possible at all, such as pay per call.

vars.name: Own agent completed share
vars.why: Our proposed threshold, not sourced. Above 3% for two months, build the gateway.

build.must: Verify agent signatures at the edge with trust tiers
build.why: Signed or registered agents earn trust tiers. Unsigned browsers pay under normal card scoring.

build.must: Write the evidence record before every payment call
build.why: A dispute without the mandate, cart and agent proof is lost by default.

build.must: Delete evidence after the rail's longest dispute window
build.why: Data protection limits storage. Your privacy lead owns the retention rule.

build.must: Idempotency key on every checkout and payment call
build.why: Agents retry on timeout, and a retry must never charge twice.

build.must: Tag every agent order with the agent platform id
build.why: Your own agent order share, against our proposed 3% trigger, decides when to build more.

build.must: Accept agentic network tokens through your existing PSP
build.why: Live agent checkout already runs on Visa and Mastercard tokens.

build.must: Score unsigned agent payments as ordinary card not present sales
build.why: Stored cards hide the agent from the issuer. Do not refuse them.

build.must: UCP adapter once agent orders pass our proposed 3% threshold
build.why: The only checkout protocol live in 90 days. A UCP adapter is a checkout state machine.

build.must: Verify signed order webhooks, one HMAC secret per platform
build.why: ACP signs with HMAC-SHA256, UCP with RFC 9421. Check timestamps too.

build.must: Discovery surface with feed, capability file and MCP server
build.why: An agent cannot buy what it cannot find.

build.must: Buyer confirms total and payment method before checkout completes
build.why: A bot signature or a ready status is not buyer permission.

build.must: Mandate verifier that cannot call the PSP
build.why: Checks the cart against the authority record. Spend caps across merchants sit buyer side.

build.must: Record what you served and ask for the mandate context
build.why: The agent platform holds what the agent saw before signing. Signatures can sit on manipulation.

build.must: Strong customer authentication when the agent mandate is set up
build.why: SCA applies at set up. Visa's live EU flow uses a passkey, no signed mandate.

build.must: Multi factor check per payment or a bank held limit
build.why: Indian rules need multiple factors per payment, and UPI Reserve Pay holds approved limits.

build.must: Published refund terms and a refund by agreement flow
build.why: On chain payments are final and x402 defines no refund or dispute process.

build.must: One HTTP 402 responder that speaks x402 and MPP
build.why: Both are live for machine pay per call and share the same shape.

build.must: Settle through a facilitator, never hold prepaid agent balances
build.why: Prepaid agent balances may be stored value that needs a licence.

build.must: Settle and serve each paid call as one atomic step
build.why: Research shows paid but denied and unpaid service attacks on x402.

build.must: Hard per agent budget enforced outside the model
build.why: Older x402 clients let a hostile server set the amount with no cap.

build.must: Meter calls and charge the card in batches
build.why: Card token minimums make sub dollar calls uneconomic one by one.

build.must: Register the buying agent and validate the supplier
build.why: The live Visa, BILL and Billtrust pilot pays invoices through a registered agent.

build.must: Buyer side platform enforces the human set spend limit
build.why: Spend caps across suppliers live with the buyer's platform or the network.

build.must: Strong customer authentication on business card payments unless exempt
build.why: SCA can apply to B2B card payments in the EU and UK unless an exemption applies.

build.must: Agreed security procedure that covers agent originated payment orders
build.why: UCC 4A binds the business for bank transfers. Whether it covers stablecoins is open.

build.must: Written terms for agent mistakes that are not fraud
build.why: Visa makes cardholders answer for enrolled agents, but disputes still use human reason codes.

build.must: Own the outcomes of every agent your business deploys
build.why: UK competition guidance makes a business responsible for what its agent does.

build.must: Review AI risk controls for each agent in production
build.why: MAS guidelines ask firms to review controls as agentic AI spreads.

build.must: Follow the payouts desk design on the linked page
build.why: Payouts use different rails and rules, covered on their own page.

patterns.name: Network token
patterns.best_for: Human present consumer checkout on card rails
patterns.breaks_on: Wrong item at the right price, fake merchants, sub dollar calls
patterns.latency: One token request, no agentic figure published
patterns.liability: Issuer holds token fraud. Visa cardholders answer for enrolled agents
patterns.one: The agent pays with a scoped token and never sees the card.
patterns.arch: Network or PSP token bound to merchant, amount and expiry. Charged on card rails with chargebacks intact. Limits cap loss but prove nothing about intent.

patterns.name: Signed mandate
patterns.best_for: Delegated, recurring and B2B purchases needing proof
patterns.breaks_on: Valid signatures over manipulated context, and no live money yet
patterns.latency: Signing at setup, then a fast local check per payment (our estimate)
patterns.liability: Evidence only, dispute resolution left out of scope
patterns.one: The user signs what the agent may buy, and the proof travels.
patterns.arch: The user signs open mandates with limits, and the agent key signs closed cart mandates inside them, as SD-JWT. A verifier checks scope, expiry and replay before payment.

patterns.name: HTTP 402 pay per call
patterns.best_for: API, data and content priced per call
patterns.breaks_on: Paid but denied outcomes, missing spend caps, no protocol refund path
patterns.latency: One extra round trip, sub second settlement target
patterns.liability: Payer carries the loss unless the seller agrees to refund
patterns.one: The server asks for payment, the agent pays and retries.
patterns.arch: Server returns 402 with a price. Wallet signs within a cap, client retries, server verifies, serves, then settles. Serve and settle must be atomic.

patterns.name: Registered agent
patterns.best_for: Agentic browsers and bot triage at the merchant edge
patterns.breaks_on: Proves the tool not the human, and tags not converged
patterns.latency: One signature check per request, keys cached
patterns.liability: Unchanged. Cloudflare says the site pays when users dispute
patterns.one: The agent signs every request so merchants can tell it from a bot.
patterns.arch: HTTP signatures checked against a network or well known key directory, with expiry, plus a nonce where the network requires one. The edge then assigns a trust tier.

patterns.name: Single use virtual card
patterns.best_for: Interim agent spend where merchants take no agentic token
patterns.breaks_on: Issuer sees a card, not an agent. Networks call it a bridge
patterns.latency: One card request on the buyer side
patterns.liability: Card rules for a human cardholder, plus program terms
patterns.one: The agent gets a card number for one purchase or budget.
patterns.arch: An issuing program mints a scoped card for the agent. The merchant sees a normal card payment. Limits live in the program, not a mandate.

patterns.name: Unrecognised agent, stored card
patterns.best_for: Nothing by design. It happens, so handle it
patterns.breaks_on: Stored cards hide the agent, so issuer agent controls never apply
patterns.liability: Normal card rules, as if the cardholder paid
patterns.one: An agentic browser pays with a saved card, and nobody sees an agent.
patterns.arch: The browser fills the normal checkout with the user's saved card. Score it as ordinary card not present, step up new merchants, tag suspected agent orders.

tree.q: Paying out to people or suppliers?
Is a machine paying per call?
Does the agent present an agentic token or a mandate?
Is the human present at payment?
Is the amount under the card floor?
Does the agent platform keep you as merchant of record?
Does a regulator require strong customer authentication?
Can the agent present a signed mandate with SCA at setup?

criteria.name: Where your buyers' agents already are
criteria.why: A surface nobody's agent uses earns nothing, however good it is.

criteria.name: Rail fit for ticket size and finality
criteria.why: Card fees kill sub dollar sales, and final rails need a refund promise.

criteria.name: Fraud and identity exposure
criteria.why: Identity and fraud risk is the top barrier merchants name in surveys.

criteria.name: Integration cost and PSP support
criteria.why: Most merchants adopt through their PSP, and adapters cost per breaking release.

criteria.name: Data and catalog readiness
criteria.why: Data readiness is the next barrier merchants name. Agents need readable catalogs.

criteria.name: Maturity for your use case
criteria.why: Live beats Pilot beats Spec, but early movers win placement.

criteria.name: Openness of governance and lock in
criteria.why: A foundation governed spec is safer than one company's roadmap.

criteria.name: Liability clarity, a gate
criteria.why: A route launches only once someone is named to carry the loss.

components.name: Agent identity verifier
components.one: Checks signed requests and registrations, then gives each agent a trust tier.

components.name: Discovery surface
components.one: Product feed, capability file and MCP server so agents can find you.

components.name: Protocol adapters
components.one: Map each protocol into the canonical model, verify webhooks, never rewrite signed artifacts.

components.name: Mandate verifier
components.one: Checks the cart against the authority record and writes evidence. Cannot move money.

components.name: Policy and risk engine
components.one: Velocity caps at this merchant, agent cohort scoring, step up thresholds and jurisdiction rules.

components.name: Canonical order and payment model
components.one: One schema for cart, credential and a thin authority record with the signed original.

components.name: Payment orchestrator
components.one: Calls the PSP or stablecoin facilitator with idempotency keys and never holds card numbers.

components.name: Evidence store
components.one: Append only record of mandate, cart and agent proof, deleted after the dispute window.

components.name: Order events and reconciliation
components.one: Sends order updates, tags every agent order and reconciles to the ledger.

components.name: Refund and dispute service
components.one: Maps evidence to network dispute responses and runs refunds on final rails.

adoption.label: x402 Foundation members, October 2026
adoption.one: Announced under the Linux Foundation in April 2026, operational launch 2026-07-14. Members passed fifty by October.

adoption.label: UCP endorsing companies listed
adoption.one: The spec site lists endorsers. It does not say who ships checkout.

adoption.label: MPP named payment methods
adoption.one: Cards, stablecoins and Lightning are listed. There is still no bank debit method.

adoption.label: x402 transactions, August to October 2026
adoption.one: 17.9 million in August, 5.1 million in October, then a rise at one settlement service.

adoption.label: Agentic share of x402 settled value
adoption.one: Between 0.6 and 7.5 percent after screens, about 5K to 11K USD a month.

adoption.label: x402 settled in October 2026
adoption.one: 5.1 million payments averaging about five cents each, on a single operator tracker.

adoption.label: MPP on Tempo, lifetime events
adoption.one: From 1,874 payers to 92 payees. Card based MPP runs off chain, uncounted.

adoption.label: Agent activity reaching checkout pages
adoption.one: Most agent visits land on product and search pages, not checkout.

adoption.label: Amazon blocks named AI agents
adoption.one: Amazon's robots.txt bars named agents from Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity.

adoption.label: European banks in controlled live Agent Pay tests
adoption.one: Mastercard's footnote names 36 banks. Pilot, not public.

adoption.label: Personal agents paying with Shop Pay
adoption.one: Muse, Claude Duet and Instinct pay with a network stand in card, never the real one.

adoption.label: Comfortable with AI buying for them
adoption.one: Kantar is the only neutral firm in the survey set.

adoption.label: Shopify AI search orders, year on year
adoption.one: Shopify says the volume is still small. Base level not disclosed.

adoption.label: Visa AI partners live
adoption.one: Visa calls agentic volume limited and very small, with Ramp bill pay generally available.

adoption.label: Trust AI to make a payment
adoption.one: Visa sponsored the poll. It gains if trust attaches to networks.

adoption.label: Alipay AI Pay, one week
adoption.one: Largest reported base, outside Western protocols. Every payment needs user approval.

adoption.label: Transactions merchants say involve agents
adoption.one: Merchant estimate, UK and US, no method given.

adoption.label: US ecommerce orders completed by agents

research.name: Beyond the Mandate
research.one: A signed approval proves the cart did not change. It does not prove the user wanted it.
research.arch: AP2 threat model. Valid signatures do not ensure intent when the context before signing is manipulated.
research.means: Keep what the agent saw before the user signed.

research.name: Zero trust checks for AP2
research.finding: Replay stopped at about 3.8 ms, in simulation
research.one: Approvals that work once and only for one shop stop copied payments, and the check is fast.
research.arch: Context binding plus consume once mandates stopped the evaluated replay and redirect attacks in simulation.
research.means: Single use approvals tied to merchant and cart.

research.name: Attacks on x402
research.finding: Up to 100 percent of paid content leaked
research.one: Pay per call can charge without serving, or serve without being paid.
research.arch: Five practical attacks plus four flaw classes on testnets and live endpoints, all disclosed to maintainers.
research.means: Settle and serve as one step, with a refund path.

research.name: Formal analysis of four protocols
research.one: A proof tool found gaps in all four major agent payment protocols.
research.arch: Tamarin models of x402, MPP, ACP and AP2. Findings are consistency gaps between authorization, payment and delivery.
research.means: Bind approval, payment and delivery at every step.

research.name: Persuasion in AI shopping
research.finding: Sponsored picks 61.2 percent, against 22.4 with search
research.one: A shopping assistant nearly tripled paid picks, and Sponsored labels did not help.
research.arch: Study of human participants. Labels did not significantly reduce sponsored selection.
research.means: Show paid placement on the approval and receipt.

research.name: Project Deal
research.one: People with weaker agents got worse prices and did not notice.
research.arch: 69 staff agents traded with each other. Outcome depended on the agent's model, and users did not spot the gap.
research.means: Record the agent model and version for disputes.

research.name: Visa benchmark
research.finding: 54 percent of failed runs still bought something
research.one: When agents got the task wrong, most still went ahead and bought.
research.arch: 22 models on shopping tasks, 42.8 percent of runs failed. Checkout and payment were not tested.
research.means: Check the cart against what the user approved.

challenges.name: Who pays, and dispute proof
challenges.one: Visa puts enrolled agents' purchases on the cardholder, Link on the user. Disputes still use human reason codes.
challenges.arch: Name the loss holder per route before launch. Write evidence before payment: mandate, cart served, agent id and key snapshot, kept for the rail's dispute window.
challenges.pain: If the agent buys the wrong thing, I cannot tell who pays me back.
challenges.working: Visa agentic rules, Amex promised cover, UK Treasury, FCA, Cloudflare coalition.
challenges.research: A valid mandate signature does not prove what the user intended.

challenges.name: Trust to press pay
challenges.one: Only 23 to 28 percent of US shoppers are comfortable letting an agent pay.
challenges.arch: Keep a human approval above a threshold, show cart and merchant before pay, and make disputes one tap. 32 percent accept agent choice with final approval.
challenges.pain: I will let it choose, but I want to approve before it pays.
challenges.working: Visa and Mastercard agent programs, Amex promised cover, six bank principles.
challenges.research: Users with weaker agents got worse deals and did not notice.

challenges.name: Telling good agents from bad
challenges.one: Merchants cannot tell a trusted agent from a bad bot, and fraud models tuned to humans misread both.
challenges.arch: Tier 2 for a signature plus mandate, or registered agent, agentic token and passkey. Score unsigned browsers as normal card sales. Send the agent signal at authorization.
challenges.pain: We cannot tell good agents from bad bots, so we block both and lose sales.
challenges.working: Visa and Mastercard Web Bot Auth, Cloudflare verified bots, Mastercard agent score.
challenges.research: Stored cards hide the agent from the issuer's risk controls.

challenges.name: Platforms shut agents out
challenges.one: Amazon bars 99 named AI agents and crawlers, and calls its own agent primary.
challenges.arch: Use sanctioned routes such as UCP endpoints, feeds and MCP servers, identify the agent, and honour merchant access files. Merchants should publish an agent access policy.
challenges.pain: The biggest store shuts my agent out, so it cannot shop where I shop.
challenges.working: Ninth Circuit Comet ruling, a Shopify storefront routing agents to UCP, network key directories.
challenges.research: Attackers already use open source agent frameworks to breach retailers and other companies.

challenges.name: Mandates outlive user intent
challenges.one: Spend limits, product scope and revocation are weakly expressed, so an agent's authority can outlast the user's wish.
challenges.arch: The agent platform or network enforces limits and expiry. The merchant checks the cart against the authority record, enforces consume once and logs revocations.
challenges.pain: I switched the agent off, and now I have to prove it.
challenges.working: AP2 open and closed mandates, Mastercard Verifiable Intent, Visa consumer instructions.
challenges.research: In simulation, consume once mandates bound to context stopped replay at 3.8 ms.

challenges.name: Wrong or steered purchases
challenges.one: Agents still buy the wrong thing, hidden prompts steer them, and LLM pitches steer users.
challenges.arch: Treat merchant content as untrusted, isolate it from cart building, check the cart against the mandate before pay, and record what the agent saw and its model version.
challenges.pain: My agent bought something I did not want, and I could not tell why.
challenges.working: Visa benchmark, PCAT defence research, x402 SDK spend caps, AP2 cart mandates.
challenges.research: Visa benchmark: 54 percent of failed runs still ended in a purchase decision.

challenges.name: Banks refuse agent access
challenges.one: Citi, Bank of America and JPMorgan keep outside agents from moving money, and banks shift risk to customers.
challenges.arch: Never ask for bank logins. Use network tokens or read only connectors, and record revocation with a timestamp the user can show. Wells Fargo requires proof from 2026-11-24.
challenges.pain: My bank says sharing my login with an agent makes me answer for it.
challenges.working: Plaid read only connectors, network agent tokens, Bank of America and Wells Fargo terms.
challenges.research: Reg E treats transfers by someone handed the access device as authorized until notice.

challenges.name: Rules assume a human
challenges.one: Payment rules expect a person to approve each payment, which slows delegated agent payments on regulated rails.
challenges.arch: Authenticate at delegation where rules allow, then step up per country: EU SCA when an agent pays or sets a merchant initiated mandate, two factors in India.
challenges.pain: We cannot offer delegated payments because the rules expect a human to approve each one.
challenges.working: HM Treasury consultation, FCA AI Live Testing, MAS 2027 consultation, NPCI reported agent protocol.
challenges.research: SCA elements assume human interaction, and PISP status for agents is open.

challenges.name: Protocol churn and integration cost
challenges.one: Specs break between releases, and every new agent surface asks merchants and payment providers to rebuild.
challenges.arch: Wait with readiness until your agent share passes our proposed 3% trigger for two months running. Then budget each adapter per breaking release, or let the PSP absorb it.
challenges.pain: Specs change under us, and every new agent surface asks us to rebuild.
challenges.working: Visa Intelligent Commerce Connect, Adyen Agentic, UCP technical councils.
challenges.research: A formal analysis found 40 undocumented consistency findings across four agent payment protocols.

challenges.name: Losing the customer and margin
challenges.one: Agent platforms may own the customer, charge up to 4 percent, and hide which sales they sent.
challenges.arch: Tag every agent order with the platform id, offer account linking so the customer record stays yours, and track each platform's fee per surface.
challenges.pain: The agent owns my customer, takes a cut, and I cannot see which sales it sent.
challenges.working: UCP identity linking, Personal Agent Protocol, Adobe referral measurement.
challenges.research: Only 37 percent of leaders have a plan to keep the direct relationship.

routes.name: Visa card, enrolled agent
routes.one: Visa's rules make the cardholder answer for an enrolled agent, as if they paid themselves.
routes.arch: Rule 4.1.23.10, added 2026-04. No agent dispute condition, so disputes run on reason codes built for human buyers.
routes.open: Will a signed mandate count as dispute evidence?

routes.name: Mastercard card
routes.one: No rule text found. Its guide says normal chargeback rights apply.
routes.arch: Developer guide: standard fraud, chargeback and dispute processes apply, and agents take on consumer checks. Rules PDF unread.
routes.open: Will Mastercard publish a rule like Visa's?

routes.name: Stripe Link agent wallet
routes.one: The user pays for every agent purchase, even a different item from the one shown.
routes.arch: Link agent wallet FAQ. Purchase Protections are US only, discretionary and silent on agents.
routes.open: How do these terms sit with card chargeback rights?

routes.name: Amex card
routes.one: Agent Purchase Protection is promised for registered agents, not yet live.
routes.arch: Cover for registered agents with authenticated intent. Announced, no live integrations found.
routes.open: When does the cover go live, and for whom?

routes.name: Card dispute, not fraud
routes.one: The merchant carries a wrong item dispute by default, unless it wins.
routes.arch: Non fraud card disputes default to the merchant. No network has an agent reason code yet.
routes.open: Will networks add an agent reason code?

routes.name: US bank login shared
routes.one: One law firm reads US rules as putting it on the customer until they revoke access.
routes.arch: Goodwin on Reg E 1005.2(m): access given to an agent counts as authorised until the bank is told, unless the bank broke its own procedure.
routes.open: Does an AI provider count as a person given the access device?

routes.name: UK online payment
routes.one: For an unauthorised online payment the payer carries no loss. This is our reading.
routes.arch: PSRs 2017 reg 77(4)(c) and (d), and 77(6) for a payee side that skipped strong checks. Our reading, not a regulator view.
routes.open: Is a payment inside the user's mandate authorised?

routes.name: Stablecoin payment
routes.one: Final on chain. The payer has no way back unless the seller refunds.
routes.arch: x402 defines no refund or dispute process. Refunds happen only by the seller's agreement.
routes.open: Who offers buyer recourse on final rails?

routes.name: Agent checked at the CDN
routes.one: Cloudflare's coalition says the site pays when a user disputes an agent purchase.
routes.arch: Trusted Agent Delegation post, 2026-11-05. Identity tiers only, no named members and no rule text.
routes.open: Will any site sign up to carry that loss?

places.name: United States
places.one: No agent law. The consumer regulator is silent, and a Fed governor asked who pays.
places.arch: No CFPB statement found by 2026-11-15. Card network rules lead, with Visa's 4.1.23.10 the only agent text.
places.next: Card networks may write the first rule

places.name: European Union
places.one: New payment law is near final but does not mention agents.
places.arch: PSR final vote planned 2026-12-14, applying about late 2028. An industry council works on agent refunds for local payment methods.

places.name: United Kingdom
places.one: Treasury asked about agent liability, and the FCA plans a trust framework.
places.arch: Treasury Question 15 closed 2026-10-06 with no response yet. Regulators say existing law applies to personal agents.

places.name: India
places.one: Two factor checks on every digital payment, with no agent text.
places.arch: RBI Authentication Directions apply from 2026-04-01. A reported agent protocol on UPI has no confirmed launch.
places.next: Launch of an agent protocol on UPI

places.name: Singapore
places.one: AI risk rules apply from 2027-10, and agent guidance goes to consultation in 2027.
places.arch: MAS AI Risk Management Guidelines issued 2026-10-07. Firms stay responsible for third party AI.

redteam.one: Our main bet held in every scenario, so nothing could prove it wrong.
redteam.arch: The thesis had no exit test, and its build trigger could not be measured.
redteam.change: Added a wait option and a trigger you can measure.

redteam.one: Building around the signed mandate put the least settled part in the core.
redteam.arch: Mandate formats still change, so a mandate centred core would churn with every spec.
redteam.change: The core keeps a thin record of five fields plus the signed original.

redteam.one: No wait option, and no world where agents suggest and people pay.
redteam.arch: The evidence points to agents that refer while people still pay, and the options ignored it.
redteam.change: Added wait with readiness, and an agents refer, people pay scenario.

redteam.one: A merchant gateway cannot cap an agent's spend at other merchants.
redteam.arch: Buyer side controls such as cross merchant spend caps sit outside the merchant's reach.
redteam.change: Spend caps across merchants move to the buyer side and the network.

redteam.one: The ranking rewarded writing specs and ignored who controls the token.
redteam.arch: Spec authorship was over weighted against control of the credential layer.
redteam.change: Players rescored with a token layer measure.

redteam.one: Virtual cards and agent browsers on stored cards were missing.
redteam.arch: Two live patterns were absent from the comparison and the decision tree.
redteam.change: Added both, with stored cards as the one to avoid.

redteam.one: Key build choices were missing, such as agent flags at authorization.
redteam.arch: Missing: agent signal in authorization, CIT and MIT, account linking, fees and amount drift.
redteam.change: Three new parameters joined the build list.

redteam.one: Two scenarios were already happening together, and none had a dated test.
redteam.arch: Scenarios overlapped and lacked falsifiable, dated kill tests.
redteam.change: Each scenario now has a dated kill test.

redteam.one: Building to the token moves lock in to the network and the payment provider.
redteam.arch: Token portability depends on the token requestor, so lock in shifts rather than disappears.
redteam.change: Kept the bet, and added a contract question on who holds the token.

redteam.one: Scoring weights had no basis, and fraud and privacy had no say.
redteam.arch: Weights were unexplained, and fraud, customer ownership and privacy were unscored.
redteam.change: Liability became a gate, and weights got a stated basis.

redteam.one: The worked example compared layers as if they were rivals.
redteam.arch: It ranked options from different stack layers against each other.
redteam.change: Rebuilt the example to compare like with like.

redteam.one: A tier rule would have refused the consumer flows that are live today.
redteam.arch: The tier 2 rule blocked live consumer flows that cannot yet meet it.
redteam.change: Relaxed the tier rule for live consumer flows.

redteam.one: Too many parameter rows, mixing choices with context.
redteam.arch: 37 rows mixed design choices, context fields and evidence fields.
redteam.change: Kept the rows, tagged each one, and the page shows only the choices.

redteam.one: The challenge ranking hid two tiers and missed churn, attribution and fees.
redteam.arch: Ties hid a two tier ranking, and three pains were missing.
redteam.change: Merged two pairs and added churn and margin challenges.

redteam.one: Tempo was counted twice and may sit inside Stripe's orbit.
redteam.arch: MPP authorship counted for both Stripe and Tempo.
redteam.change: Tempo left the startup list.

redteam.one: Cloudflare's coalition launch was missed.
redteam.arch: A dated market move inside the window was not scored.
redteam.change: Scored as a move, since it names no members yet.

redteam.one: Some answers ended in flows nobody can build today.
redteam.arch: Several leaves pointed to flows with no shipped implementation.
redteam.change: Changed the tree endings to flows you can build.

redteam.one: Saying every payment can be defended overclaimed, and nobody owned privacy.
redteam.arch: ADR-4 overclaimed defensibility and gave the evidence store no privacy owner.
redteam.change: Softened the claim, and the evidence store got a privacy owner.

redteam.one: The speed target for agent checks has never been tested.
redteam.arch: The 300 ms p95 target has no production measurement behind it.
redteam.change: Marked as a target. Still open.

redteam.one: Small mismatches between sections.
redteam.arch: Internal slips across sections 1.3, 2.3 and 8.
redteam.change: Fixed across the doc.

decide.name: Tag agent orders
decide.one: Mark every order an agent placed, so you can see your own share.
decide.arch: Tag P28 on every order. Your agent completed share (V17) is what fires the build trigger in ADR-1.
decide.trigger: Without the tag, our proposed 3% trigger cannot fire.

decide.name: Name who pays
decide.one: Before launch, write down who carries a wrong agent purchase on each payment route.
decide.arch: Map each route to its loss holder and basis, network rule, terms or chargeback rights, before go live.
decide.trigger: Any agent order on a new route.

decide.name: Evidence before payment
decide.one: Save the purchase record before money moves, and keep it only while disputes can happen.
decide.arch: Write evidence before the PSP call, then append the result. Retention is the longest dispute window of the rail (V18).

decide.name: Trust tiers for agents
decide.one: Let agents browse freely, and ask for more proof before they pay.
decide.arch: Tier 0 browse, tier 1 cart, tier 2 pay. Tier 2 needs a signature plus mandate, or a registered agent, agentic token and passkey.

decide.name: Build to the token
decide.one: Keep your payment provider until agent orders pass our proposed trigger, then build.
decide.arch: Below the trigger, wait with readiness. Above it, canonical model plus adapters, or the PSP if it exports evidence.
decide.trigger: Our proposed 3% trigger for two months running.

decide.name: Pay per call apart
decide.one: Keep tiny machine payments on their own path, away from card checkout.
decide.arch: HTTP 402 calls settle through a facilitator. Budgets sit in the buyer's wallet, never as prepaid balances you hold.
